title: Level 1: Position the Cricket Ball
description: Welcome to the cricket game! The ball is at the bowler's hand. We need to get it to the batting crease to start the match.

hints.concept: Use translateX() to move horizontally. Positive values move to the right.

question: Move the ball 200px to the right.

title: Level 2: Spin the Ball
description: Good! The ball is in position. But a good bowler adds spin to make it harder to hit. Let's give it some rotation.

hints.concept: rotate() takes degrees (deg). Positive numbers rotate clockwise.

question: Rotate the ball 45 degrees.

title: Level 3: Make the Ball Visible
description: Perfect spin! But the camera crew says the ball is too small on screen. The viewers at home can barely see it.

hints.concept: scale() resizes the element. 1.0 is normal size, 1.5 is 50% larger.

question: Scale the ball to 1.5 times larger.

title: Level 4: Set Up the Bowling Position
description: Great! Now the director wants a perfect shot. The ball needs to be at the right distance and the right size for the close-up camera angle.

hints.concept: You can apply multiple transforms by separating them with a space.

question: Move the ball 150px right and double its size.

title: Level 5: Create the Perfect Delivery Stance
description: The bowler is ready for the match-winning delivery! This needs perfect positioning, maximum spin, and camera-ready sizing all at once.

hints.concept: Order matters! Translations are affected by rotation. Usually translate first.

question: Move 120px right, rotate 180 degrees, and scale to 1.8x.

title: Level 6: Animate the Delivery
description: The ball jumps instantly! That looks unrealistic. Real cricket balls travel smoothly through the air from bowler to batsman.

hints.concept: Use transition to smooth out changes. Syntax: property duration.

question: Add a 2-second transition.

title: Level 7: Perfect the Bowling Speed
description: Better! But fast bowlers don't move at constant speed. They start the run-up slow, accelerate in the middle, then release smoothly.

hints.concept: Timing functions control acceleration. ease-in-out starts and ends slowly.

question: Make it 1.5 seconds with ease-in-out timing.

title: Level 8: Add Ball Visibility Effects
description: The ball is traveling fast now! Add some motion blur effect - the ball should fade slightly as it grows and moves, just like in slow-motion replays.

hints.concept: Separate multiple transitions with a comma.

question: Transition transform over 2s ease-out, opacity over 1s linear.
expectedCSS: transform: translateX(180px) scale(1.6); opacity: 0.7; transition: transform 2s ease-out, opacity 1s linear;

title: Level 9: Make the Ball Bounce
description: The ball hits the pitch! Every good delivery bounces once before reaching the batsman. Let's add that bounce effect.

hints.concept: For animations, specify the keyframe name and duration.

question: Apply the 'bounce' animation for 2 seconds.

title: Level 10: Continuous Ball Spin
description: Nice bounce! But the ball stops spinning after one rotation. In real cricket, the ball keeps spinning throughout its flight.

hints.concept: Add 'infinite' to make the animation repeat forever.

question: Make 'spin' animation run for 1s and repeat infinitely.

title: Level 11: Ball Moving Back and Forth
description: It's practice time! The coach wants the ball to move back and forth between bowler and batsman for practice drills.

hints.concept: Use 'alternate' to play the animation forward then backward.

question: Make 'slide' run 2s, infinite, and alternate direction.

title: Level 12: Realistic Ball Wobble
description: The commentators notice something! The ball's seam is causing it to wobble in the air - this is what makes it so hard to hit!

hints.concept: Combine timing (ease-in-out) with iteration and direction.

question: Apply 'wobble' for 1.8s with ease-in-out, infinite, alternate.

title: Level 13: Delayed Power Shot
description: The batsman sees the ball coming! He winds up his bat, takes a breath, then BOOM - a powerful shot! We need a delay before the action.

hints.concept: The delay value comes AFTER the duration value.

question: Apply 'pulse' 2s, ease-in, 0.5s delay, infinite, alternate.

title: Level 14: Complex Shot Animation
description: SIX! The ball is flying through the air with incredible trajectory - spinning, scaling, and fading all at once as it soars toward the boundary!

hints.concept: The complex animation handles position. The other properties are static starts.

question: Apply 'complex' 3s, ease-in-out, 0.3s delay, infinite, alternate.
expectedCSS: animation: complex 3s ease-in-out 0.3s infinite alternate; transform: rotate(0deg); opacity: 1;

title: Level 15: Master Shot - The Final Delivery
description: This is it - the final ball of the match! Everything must be perfect: the position, the spin, the size, the timing. The entire stadium holds its breath...
answer: translateX(100px) rotate(45deg) scale(1.4) AND master 2.5s ease-in-out 0.2s infinite alternate

hints.concept: Define the static transform first. Then add the master animation below it.

question: Transform: move 100px right, rotate 45deg, scale 1.4x. Animate: 'master' 2.5s, ease-in-out, 0.2s delay, infinite, alternate.
expectedCSS: transform: translateX(100px) rotate(45deg) scale(1.4); animation: master 2.5s ease-in-out 0.2s infinite alternate; opacity: 0.85;
